Comments: On November 21, 2024, the Department conducted a restoration inspection of the Diamond 3 OG Well in Nicholson Township, Fayette County. The access road appears to be unrestored at the time of this inspection. The Department requests that the Operator restore the access road or provide the Department with the following information if it is to remain.1. The completion of plugging for this well reportedly occurred on 3/13/2024 therefore the well site shall be restored no later than 12/12/2024 per current regulations.Based on today's inspection, the WSRR is not approved. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/01/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 987242
Permit API: 081-21879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/01/2023
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after multiple releases on Pad B for which violations remain outstanding. Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. The completions operations have ceased on Pad B and the snubbing rigs and their associated equipment have been removed from the pad. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad B. A representative from Creston Environmental was present on location as well. A crew was working on installing the GPUs on the pad. Trenches were being dug for the flow lines which will run from the well heads to the GPUs on the west side of the pad. A large trench was present at the well heads. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/06/2026 to BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC in Springfield Township, Bradford county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/06/2026
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8266449
Permit API: 015-24012
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/06/2026
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Blackhill Energy's Lee North well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 3/6/2026 at 0900 hours. The weather was 41 degrees F with cloudy skies and fog. A new Act 9 sign has been installed at the site entrance (photo #1). Site plans and an inspection log are held in the mailbox by the gate.New Spud dates for 3/3/2026 were recored for the Lee North 2H, 4H, 6H and 8H wells. A top-hole rig was observed drilling for the new wells' conductor casings. Topsoil has been piled on top of the pad's fill and cut slopes. The construction contractor plans to come back to rework the topsoil onto the slopes and construct the perimeter channels. Additional work is also necessary for the sediment basin. Recent thawing, snow melt and heavy rainfall has caused erosion and slumping on the pad's cut and fill slopes, stormwater channels and piled topsoils. Evidence of erosion can be seen in photos #5-7. Sediment laden fluids were observed flowing through the temporarily constructed stormwater channels and entering the sediment basin. The fluids in the basin then flowed into the skimmer and out of basin's outflow pipe. Sediment laden fluids were observed escaping the site's limit-of-disturbance (LOD) and into Wetland 4J (PEM) (photos #8 and 12). Photo #12 shows the observed sedimentation present in Wetland 4J. The planned rip rap apron below the sediment basin outflow pipe has not yet been constructed.The sediment laden fluids eventually flow downslope into Mill Creek. The DEP observed Mill Creek upstream and downstream of the sedimentation and Mill Creek appeared more turbid downstream of the sedimentation. Samples for Standard Analysis Code (SAC) 046 were collected from Mill Creek both upstream and downstream of the observed sedimentation. Photos #13 and 14 show samples #0983-523 and 524 next to the sample locations. The samples were collected to determine if Mill Creek was also impacted by the sedimentation.Based on the observed sediment laden fluids escaping the site's LOD and entering Wetland 4J, the following violations are cited against API #015-24012 at this time:25 Pa. Code 102.4(b)135 P.S. 691.401A representative with Blackhill Energy met onsite during this inspection. I explained my findings and the Blackhill Energy representative contacted the construction contractor to address the issues noted. The contractor planned to install some rock below the basin's outflow pipe to slow down some of the fluids and add silt sock to contain the sedimentation. I departed the site at 1150 hours.

Present were Rosie Wise (DEP Environmental Trainee) and myself. This inspection follows up to IR 4168852, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed during the inspection:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they still lack compliant secondary containment to 78a.64(a), as is required at unconventional well sites (photos 4, 6, and 7). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (photo 10). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (photos 3 and 11). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team. The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (photos 9 and 12). A violation was issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C). The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (photos 5 and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4168852 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 12/14/2022
Comments: On Wednesday, 12/14/2022, I conducted a routine inspection of the Diversified Production, LLC McIntyre 1 well, permit number 005-29235. The well is located in the woods off of Coal Bank Road in Gilpin township, Armstrong county. The well is in production and had a reported production of 5,341.89 mcf for 2021. There is a well id tag attached to the well head and a well site id sign is posted on the production chart box. The site is restored, but the operator has not maintained the E and S BMP's for the site and there is an area of standing/ponded water on the access road near the site entrance (see picture #8) that needs to be addressed. The site cannot be considered stabilized due to this area and also the area of dead vegetation that was caused by brine being sprayed from a broken pipe onto the brine tank and ground. The brine tank itself is stable and appears to be structurally sound, but the pipe into the brine tank from the gas separator has rusted through and broken off, spraying brine onto the outside of the tank and onto the ground (see pictures #6 and #7). The amount of brine released appears to be less than 1 bbl. These conditions have resulted in violations to 25 PA Code 78.57(a), 25 PA Code 78.54, SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1) and CSL 402(b) being cited. Although there were no violations cited, the deficiencies on the access road need to be addressed while the operator is addressing the conditions that resulted in the cited violations.

Violation Code: 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 842735
Permit API: 059-27350
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-02-21
Comments: On Tuesday February 19, 2019 I received notification of a produced water release at the Magnum Well Site located in Center Township, Greene County. The release had occurred and was reported to the Department on February 17, 2019. On Tuesday morning I spoke on the telephone with Mr. Corey Giles from EQT Production Company (EQT) regarding details of the incident and the remediation. On February 19 and February 21, I. conducted incident inspections to further assess the situation. The February 21 inspection was conducted after receiving additional requested details from Mr. Giles. On February 17, EQT representatives discovered the release which resulted from a dump valve wash-out. It was estimated that approximately 25-30 gallons was released from the unit as a result of the wash-out. This occurred on the "B" side of the unit and impacted the well pad in front, along side and behind the unit. EQT's remediation contractor, SPSI, excavated the impacted materials for off-site disposal and backfilled the excavated areas. The excavation in front of the GPU was approximately five (5) feet by 24 feet and was approximately six (6) inches in depth at the deepest point. The excavation on the side was approximately five (5) feet by 12 feet and was also six (6) inches and less in depth. The excavation behind the units was approximately five (5) feet by 100 feet and ranged in depth between six (6) inches and 18 inches due to some softer spots that were encountered. Given the excavation dimensions, it appears that no native materials were impacted. As of October 2016, all production equipment is required to be within secondary containment in accordance with 25 Pa. Code, Section 78a.64a(b). These GPUs were not utilizing secondary containment. Due to a recent agreement to obtain compliance with 78a.64a(b) between the Department and EQT, the site is currently In Compliance with Policy (ICP) relative to secondary containment use with production equipment. The release of produced water and impact to the well pad surface is a violation of 25 Pa. Code, Sections 78a.54 and 78a.57a, as well as 35 P.S. Section 6018.301. The operator should respond in accordance with the directions provided in this notice.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/02/2022 to TURM OIL INC in Cherryhill Twp, Indiana county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TURM OIL INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/02/2022
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 957723
Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

Comments: On December 18, 2025, the Department conducted a follow-up inspection to IR 4103246 at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. A violation that was issued in IR 4088070 was left outstanding in IR 4103246, for failure to restore the well site by 10/30/2025, in accordance with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A. The Department requested an NOV Response to IR 4088070 from the operator by December 4, 2025. However, no formal response to IR 4088070 has been received to-date from the operator.The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites."Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed:The Act 9 sign has been removed from the entrance of the pre-existing access road (photo 1). The access road is to remain unrestored, as it predates construction of the well site (photos 2-4). Temporary stabilization is inconsistent throughout the former well site, as large areas of exposed soil were observed on the slopes at the northern and southern site boundaries (photos 7, 8, 15, and 16). No loose sediment was observed in the rock-lined channels that empty into the pre-existing Sediment Trap (photos 9 and 12). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed at the northern and southern boundaries (photos 9, 11, 17, and 19). The improperly installed super silt fence which was identified in IR 4084771 remains, with the fabric having completely detached and fallen to the ground (photo 18). No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation was observed on site during this inspection. No restoration plans were found on site during this inspection.The Department continues to recommend that the operator reassess whether the E and S controls installed on site are adequate for this well site restoration.The Department also continues to recommend that the operator apply additional temporary stabilization where bare soil is exposed.Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4088070 shall remain outstanding.

SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/24/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 989581
Permit API: 081-21907
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/24/2023
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions at the site after the reported release of produced fluid to the well pad on 3/3/23. The frac is still on-going on the pad. I met with company man Wade Adams upon arriving on location. In the area where the release from 3/3/23 sprayed produced fluid onto the well pad in the south travel lane and southeast of the MASS, puddles of fluid had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 852 uS/cm. Fluid at the outlet of the north stormwater channel had an EC of 478 uS/cm. The well site secondary containment appears to be in good condition. No holes or crushed berms were observed. A vacuum truck was present on the pad which was sucking up fluid from the secondary containment. Violations remain outstanding from the reported release of produced fluid to the pad surface on 3/3/23.
